description: Frontend: first-run name-entry dialog shown right after a brand-new monster is hatched, plus a rename affordance from the StatsPanel header to change the name later. Both open the same accessible dialog (mirroring the #20/#32 reset-confirm pattern), validate with the shared isValidMonsterName helper, and persist the chosen name via api.saveMonster so a reload keeps it. Depends on FEAT-001 (imports isValidMonsterName/normalizeMonsterName/MONSTER_NAME_MAX_LENGTH from @ddm/shared).
steps: i18n (packages/frontend/src/i18n.ts): add new keys to JA_MESSAGES AND the matching EN_MESSAGES entries (both required or build fails). Suggested keys/strings (keep JA natural, EN parity): 'name.firstRunTitle' (JA '名前をつけよう' / EN 'Name your monster'), 'name.renameTitle' (JA '名前を変更' / EN 'Rename'), 'name.label' (JA 'なまえ' / EN 'Name'), 'name.placeholder' (JA 'なまえを入力（1〜12文字）' / EN 'Enter a name (1-12 chars)'), 'name.save' (JA '決定' / EN 'Save'), 'name.skip' (JA 'スキップ' / EN 'Skip') for first-run, 'name.cancel' (JA 'キャンセル' / EN 'Cancel') for rename, 'name.validation' (JA '1〜12文字で入力してください（空白のみは不可）' / EN 'Please enter 1-12 characters (not blank).'), 'name.renameButton' (JA '名前を変更' / EN 'Rename'), 'name.renameButtonAria' (JA '名前を変更' / EN 'Rename monster'). Place them in a clearly commented 'Monster naming (issue #36)' block. Do NOT alter any existing key's value.

useMonster.ts: add a way to rename and persist. Add to UseMonsterState: `rename: (name: string) => Promise<void>` and a boolean `needsName` (true right after a fresh hatch so App can auto-open the first-run dialog). In the mount effect, when the 404 hatch path runs (loaded===null branch), set a flag so needsName becomes true after the fresh baby is committed; when getMonster returns an existing monster, needsName stays false. Implement rename(name): no-op if monster is null or busy; normalize via normalizeMonsterName and guard with isValidMonsterName (ignore invalid input defensively); build next = { ...current, name: normalized, lastUpdatedAt: Date.now() }; commit optimistically then api.saveMonster and commit saved, with the same try/catch error handling shape as runCareAction (setError on failure). Expose a `dismissNeedsName` (or have rename/skip clear it). Keep DEFAULT_MONSTER_NAME behavior: the fresh baby is still created with 'でじたん' so skipping leaves a working default name.

Create packages/frontend/src/components/NameDialog.tsx: a controlled accessible dialog component. Props: open-driven usage is handled by parent conditional render; props { title: string; initialName: string; mode: 'firstRun' | 'rename'; onSubmit: (name: string) => void; onClose: () => void }. Render role='alertdialog' aria-modal='true' aria-label={title}, a labelled <input> (associate <label> via htmlFor/id, or aria-label from 'name.label'), live validation message (role alert / aria-live) using isValidMonsterName, maxLength set generously but rely on validation for the real bound, a primary Save button (disabled when invalid) and a secondary button (Skip for firstRun, Cancel for rename). Mirror App.tsx reset dialog focus management: focus the input on open (useEffect + ref), Escape calls onClose, a simple focus trap cycling between the focusable controls, and restore focus to the opener on close (opener focus restore can live in the parent like closeResetConfirm does). Use useI18n() t() for all strings. No JSX-time new deps.

Wire first-run + rename in App.tsx: track dialog state e.g. const [nameDialog, setNameDialog] = useState<null | { mode: 'firstRun' | 'rename' }>(null). Open firstRun automatically when game.needsName becomes true (useEffect). Provide a rename trigger button in the StatsPanel header area (pass an onRename callback into StatsPanel, or render a small ✎ button in StatsPanel that calls a prop). On submit: call game.rename(name) then close + clear needsName; on firstRun skip/close: clear needsName (keep default name) and restore focus; on rename cancel: just close and restore focus to the rename trigger. Follow the existing resetTriggerRef focus-restore approach. Ensure the dialog is only one of reset-confirm or name-dialog open at a time is not required, but keep z-index/overlay consistent.

StatsPanel.tsx: add a small rename control in the
next to the

{monster.name}

. Add an optional prop `onRename?: () => void`; render a

styles.css: add styles for the name dialog (reuse/extend the .reset-confirm look for consistency: overlay/box, actions row) and a compact .rename-btn. Any entrance animation MUST be disabled under the existing @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) blocks (add a rule there if you add an animation). Do not change existing selectors' meaning.

Verify name propagation: StatsPanel header h2 reads monster.name (live), BattlePanel playerName={game.monster.name}, SpeechBubble/chat read current name via useMonster. Because rename commits a new monster object through commit(), all four surfaces (StatsPanel header, BattlePanel playerName, SpeechBubble, chat api.chat monsterName) reflect the new name on next render. After a rename, a page reload re-fetches via api.getMonster and shows the persisted name (DynamoDB).

Tests: in packages/frontend/src/game-ui.test.ts add dependency-free tests (no DOM): assert i18n parity for all new keys (every new MessageKey has a non-empty ja and en entry in MESSAGES) following the existing MESSAGES/t import at top of the file; and (optionally) re-export validation behavior checks are already in shared. Keep DOM/React out of this test file. Confirm total frontend tests >= 62 after additions.

Full verification: export PATH; `npm run build` (tsc for frontend will fail if any new i18n key lacks an EN entry, catching parity bugs); `npm test` (shared) and `npm test -w @ddm/frontend` both pass.
acceptance_criteria: On first load of a brand-new monster (getMonster 404 -> hatch), an accessible name dialog appears automatically with the input focused; Escape or Skip closes it leaving the default name 'でじたん'; entering a valid 1..12 name and Save persists it (api.saveMonster) and the StatsPanel header shows it.

A rename control in the StatsPanel header opens the same dialog pre-filled with the current name; saving a new valid name updates the header, BattlePanel playerName, speech bubble, and chat monsterName, and persists via api.saveMonster.
The dialog shows a clear JA/EN validation message and disables Save for empty/whitespace-only/>12-char input, using the shared isValidMonsterName helper.
All new i18n keys have both ja and en entries (build passes) and existing keys are byte-identical.
`npm run build` succeeds; `npm test` (shared) passes; `npm test -w @ddm/frontend` passes with total >= 62.
Any dialog animation is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
verification: export PATH="/opt/toolchains/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.3/bin:$PATH"; from repo root run `npm run build` and confirm success (also validates i18n EN parity via tsc).
Run `npm test -w @ddm/frontend` and confirm all tests pass with count >= 62.
Run `npm test` and confirm shared tests still pass.
Read NameDialog.tsx and App.tsx wiring to confirm input is focused on open, Escape closes, and focus is restored to the opener; confirm rename commits through useMonster so all name surfaces update.
findings: Implemented. Added 10 i18n keys (ja+en parity) under a 'Monster naming (issue #36)' block in i18n.ts. useMonster.ts gained needsName (set true on the 404 hatch path), dismissNeedsName, and rename(name) which normalizes/validates via shared helpers then optimistic commit -> api.saveMonster -> commit(saved), matching runCareAction's error handling. New NameDialog.tsx mirrors the reset-confirm a11y pattern: role=alertdialog aria-modal, input focused+selected on open, Escape/Enter handling, focus trap over input/save/secondary, Save disabled via isValidMonsterName, live role=alert validation message (shown only after typing). App.tsx auto-opens the firstRun dialog from game.needsName, provides openRenameDialog + renameTriggerRef for focus restore on rename close, and renders NameDialog. StatsPanel.tsx header gained a .rename-btn (✎, aria-label from name.renameButtonAria) driven by onRename + renameButtonRef. styles.css added overlay/box/input/actions + .rename-btn styles with name-dialog-in entrance animation disabled under prefers-reduced-motion. Name propagation verified: rename commits a new Monster object so StatsPanel h2, BattlePanel playerName, SpeechBubble, and chat monsterName all reflect it. Build passes (tsc parity gate green). Tests: shared 52 pass, frontend 63 pass (baseline 62) including a new naming-keys parity test. Pre-existing unrelated 1-line package-lock.json change left untouched/unstaged.
